changes.after: Türk Telekomünikasyon A.Ş. is a corporation which provides a wide range of technological services. The internship was completed at this institution. The internship project named PixelProof had some goals to achieve. One of them was making a detector which can differentiate AI generated images from real images and find areas edited by AI. Another goal was to reduce false alerts, such as classifying an image as AI generated even if it is real. There were several methods used in this project. Experiment results were recorded, and new steps were decided according to these results. The project produced a web demo which includes a system that classifies images. In addition, the web demo was designed with a user-friendly interface. False alerts like classifying a real image as AI generated decreased on the development data. However, this does not indicate that results are fully reliable. There were some challenges. One of them was the difficulty of detecting specific areas manipulated by an AI generator due to data problems and the way AI generators edit images. These problems contributed to this part of the project remaining experimental. For future development, the system should be tested on datasets not used during development, and new actions should be decided according to the results.

changes.before: The main purpose of this Internship project called PixelProof is whether the detected photograph is AI generated or AI manipulated. This project contains two modules. First one is Module1. This module simply looks at the whole image and classifies this image as AI generated or real photograph. Second one is Module2. This module looks at specific areas of the image and tries to detect AI touched areas, but this module remains experimental. One of the major goals of this project is to avoid incorrect labeling, such as labeling real image as an AI generated image. Results of the project improved on the development data however, there are no guarantees that the result is fully trustworthy. The main result is a web demo which allows users to upload images supported by user friendly interface.

Next step was to train a CNN model (small CNN) and investigate the results. This model showed good performance in the test set and accuracy was 96.75%, but in a different dataset which does not include CIFAKE images, the performance of the model dropped, and accuracy decreased to 77.1%. These results showed that performance changed on a different dataset. Later checks found differences in image format and size between real and AI images. The images were converted to a common JPEG format and cropped into squares, and the test was repeated. There was no clear drop in AUC after these changes, so this check did not prove that those differences caused the original performance gap (Keleş, 2026, E1 and E10).

changes.before: One of the main problems of this project was misclassification. This misclassification includes two types. The first type is false positive which means that a real image is considered as AI generated. The second type is false negative which means AI generated images do not get recognized by the model. There are some possible solutions, but there might be performance drop in other metrics. For instance, when more AI generated images are added and labeled as ai generated, there might be performance increase in AI detection. However, detection of real images performance might drop down. Another factor is image features such as format, size, compression level. These factors may lead the model make mistakes. Therefore, these image features should be optimized.
changes.after: One of the main problems of this project was misclassification. This misclassification includes two types. The first type is false positive which means that a real image is considered as AI generated. The second type is false negative which means AI generated images do not get recognized by the model. There are some possible solutions, but there might be performance drop in other metrics. For instance, when more images are classified as AI generated, AI detection may increase. However, more real images may also be incorrectly classified as AI generated. Another factor is image features such as format, size, compression level. These factors may lead the model make mistakes. Therefore, these image features should be optimized.
